newsletters.subject: 🎙️ How I AI: Meta Muse Wonder + How Brooke Lacey is scaling video with AI
newsletters.why: Claire Vo benchmarks Meta's new 'Muse Wonder' model across ~20 real-world agentic tasks (billing support, inbox triage, computer use, email writing, coding, design, video editing). Finds it the strongest agentic model at its price tier — ranked first on billing-ticket resolution, inbox triage, computer use, email writing; resisted a prompt-injection attempt; 'active focus' capability correlates time-spent with output quality on long-running tasks. Weaknesses: poor frontend design, incomplete prototypes (80% scaffolding then broken interactions). Direct evaluation data on a frontier-adjacent agentic model — high wiki actionability for agentic-benchmarking and prompt-injection-resistance coverage. New model 'Muse Wonder' follows the existing Muse Spark / Muse Glimmer family (Meta Superintelligence Labs).
recommended_actions: Scrape full post from lennysnewsletter.com to wiki/raw/articles/ (body paragraphs already extracted this run).
Create entities/muse-wonder.md (or concepts/ entry) for the new Meta Muse Wonder model — validate tags in SCHEMA.md first; cross-link from muse-spark / muse-glimmer / meta-muse-spark.
The Brooke Lacey video-scaling segment is a workflow/practice piece — low standalone wiki value; fold into Lenny's/podcast context only if relevant.
Note the prompt-injection-resistance finding as an evaluation datapoint if concepts/prompt-injection.md exists (grep first).
newsletters.caveat: How I AI is a practical 'how people use AI' podcast; the Muse Wonder eval is the wiki-relevant core. Frontend-design and email-style observations are reviewer opinion, not benchmark data — attribute as Claire Vo's testing, not objective fact.
